tagline: Accelerating the energy transition across Europe and North America through renewable capacity expansion and grid modernization.
hero_kpi_rationale: EDP is a pure-play renewable energy player in Europe and North America, with a clear growth trajectory in solar and wind. This KPI captures the core of its growth and decarbonization strategy.

kpis.name: Installed Renewable Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total power output from operational wind and solar parks.
kpis.description: Installed capacity in renewable energy (wind + solar) as of end-2025. EDP is focusing on rapid expansion in the United States and Brazil.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by solar in the U.S. and Iberia.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.description: Consolidated EBITDA in 2025, driven by networks and renewables.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth supported by electricity demand and grid operations.

kpis.name: Investments (Capex)
kpis.explanation: Annual capital expenditures for new infrastructure.
kpis.description: Total capex in 2025, with a €3.0 Bn investment plan announced for the Portuguese distribution grid (2026–2030).
kpis.signal: Marked acceleration in investments, particularly in Portugal.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin, benefiting from the low cost variability of renewables.
kpis.signal: Improvement linked to the ramp-up of low-cost renewable assets.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: Total headcount as of end-2025, reflecting disciplined human resource management.
kpis.signal: Stable workforce despite growth, indicating operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Renewables Investment Share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of total capex dedicated to renewable energy.
kpis.description: In 2025, 60% of total capex was allocated to renewables, primarily in the U.S. and Iberia.
kpis.signal: Clear priority given to green growth.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $2.405 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.827 Bn in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 71.9% in the latest year.

kpis.name: North America EBITDA Share
kpis.explanation: Contribution of North American operations to operating profit.
kpis.description: In 2025, 60% of EBITDA came from North America. This share is expected to reach 68% by 2028.
kpis.signal: Geographic transformation of the group toward the U.S.

kpis.name: Network Investment Portugal
kpis.explanation: Planned investment amount in the Portuguese distribution grid.
kpis.description: EDP will invest €3.0 Bn between 2026 and 2030 in the distribution grid, +70% vs previous period.
kpis.signal: Major acceleration to strengthen resilience after storms.

risks.title: Dependence on electricity grid regulation
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for EDP: networks represent 31% of 2025 EBITDA and are fully dependent on regulatory frameworks (Portugal 2026-2029, Spain 2026-2031, Brazil until 2027-2030). Moderate language but central position in the 2026-28 strategy (€7Bn net investments). Stable trend with displayed regulatory visibility.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks affecting supply chains
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language on Ukraine/Middle East conflicts, logistical disruptions, and energy volatility. Position at the beginning of the document (section 3.1.1) indicates strategic importance. EDP operates in Europe, North/South America, and Asia-Pacific, exposed to these risks. Trend increasing with mention of 'sustained geopolitical fragmentation'.

risks.title: U.S. federal regulatory uncertainty on renewable energy
risks.score_rationale: Explicit warning language: 'significant policy disruption in 2025' and 'regulatory uncertainty remains'. EDP Renewables represents 39% of 2025 EBITDA and 62% of gross investments in 2025 (€3.9Bn). North America = 30% of installed capacity. Trend increasing with executive actions and federal policy revisions.

risks.title: Occupational health and safety in operations and subcontracting
risks.score_rationale: Strong language: 'not acceptable', 'Zero Serious Injuries and Fatalities' as objective. Three contractor fatalities in 2025 despite 56% improvement in SIF. Position at the beginning of the document (Management Statement) indicates strategic priority. High risk of reputational damage, litigation, and civil liability.

risks.title: Dependence on long-term contracts and capacity auctions
risks.score_rationale: EDP targets 80% of EBITDA in A-rated, regulated markets and long-term contracts (2028). Moderate but strategic language: 'distinctive and resilient portfolio'. Risk of concentration on existing contracts and dependence on future auctions (Brazil, USA). Stable trend with displayed visibility.

risks.title: Project permitting risks and commissioning delays
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language on 'Federal permitting for wind and solar projects has faced significant policy disruption'. EDP plans 2.1 GW of additions in 2025 (100% renewables/BESS) with delays of 1-3 years. Risk of delays on 322 MW under construction (2026-2029). Trend increasing with federal disruptions mentioned.

risks.title: Electricity and commodity price volatility
risks.score_rationale: Moderate language but explicit context: 'volatility in energy and commodity markets' due to geopolitical conflicts. EDP generated 64.2 TWh in 2025 with 10% thermal (CCGT) for flexibility services. Stable trend but sensitivity to external shocks. Margin risk on unhedged contracts.

risks.title: Curtailment and grid integration risks in Latin America
risks.score_rationale: Explicit language: 'regulation is expected to address curtailment impact on renewables' in Brazil. EDP Espírito Santo and EDP São Paulo represent 4% of installed capacity. Risk of revenue reduction if curtailment is not compensated. Stable trend with regulation in evolution.

ai_positioning.summary: EDP mentions the acceleration of electricity demand driven by AI (data centers), but does not position AI as a core technological lever for its operations or services.
evidence: Global electricity demand is accelerating driven by AI, industrial electrification, and electric mobility
rapid expansion of data centers across the U.S.
AI leadership driving surging electricity demand
